visualReview.notes: All nine current portable views inspected, including two new portal close-ups. Rectangular stone aperture, physical reveals, threshold steps and inset arched metal grille replace the solid block/painted fill. Existing carved accents remain generalized. Whole compound is visible on original source-native hill; roofs, towers, guest houses and pool retained.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: All nine current shared-material views inspected, including portal details and mapped overlay. Stone/metal surfaces bind consistently and real recess casts shade. Original placement/transform and unload pass. The flat shared fixture clips lower compound volumes below its zero plane; original source-ground portable/medium-fi views carry the vertical site context. Flat fixture does not certify ground levels.

mediumFiReview.notes: All 21 current version-2 frames inspected across light/quality, source-native hill context, front/back, portal details and four forced levels. Actual rectangular recess/threshold survives all levels; street/close include physical grille bars and arched fan. Existing compound silhouette and stepped masses retained. Synthetic neighbors are style evidence.

geographicReview.notes: Original mapped Casa Grande, three guest houses, Roman Pool and Neptune controls retained. Anchor [-121.16806000471115,35.685240350260685], heading -1.3197933216173452 and original reference [0,3] unchanged. Provider-relative datum 492.9056 m, source range -18.29635..0.94839 m and original stepped levels retained byte-for-byte; no ground fitting, flattening or new cutout. New portal uses the existing +3.8 m main-house offset and original opening proportions. Source-native hill views inspected; shared flat fixture establishes transform/overlay but clips lower compound and cannot establish vertical fit. Approximate source-relative exterior placement, not surveyed paving/foundation levels or certification of another live host field.

fidelityReview.scope: Coordinated mapped castle compound exterior with visible Casa Grande facade/towers, Neptune temple and newly physical entrance portal; hidden sides and garden ornament simplified.
fidelityReview.notes: Started with cleared Qualla corpus and inspected local Daderot grounds original; that photo does not show the portal. Two exact native Daderot own-work CC0 originals then inspected: full Casa Grande facade and Neptune temple. Primary creator grants/revisions and original SHA-1/SHA-256 bound. Prior CC exteriors and uncertain historical aerial excluded as current controls. New rectangular portal has real stone jamb/head depth, threshold steps, inset metal grille/arched fan and opaque inner boundary. It replaces the solid block and filled arch overlay. Existing body/towers/roofs, mapped compound footprint and source levels retained. The 0.55 m recess, width/heights, threshold rise, fine carvings, tile details, hidden facades, guest-house roofs and exact modern condition are photographic/conservative approximations. Pool temple is broadly supported by the second original; unseen compound details are not newly measured. No navigable interior, civil survey or embedded source pixels.

runtimeLodReview.notes: 683/2675/15747/25427 triangles, 1/4/4/4 draws pass strict budgets. All levels have actual rectangular recess/threshold; street/close retain physical gate bars and metal fan. Existing compound silhouettes retained. Error bounds are authoring estimates.

geometryValidation.notes: Targeted generation/import/exact regeneration, asset integrity, strict LOD/material budgets and source/imported normals/winding/UVs pass. Actual entrance air/backing, threshold coverage/steps, stone jamb/lintel and grille bar/gap controls pass. Low facade band was split around the opening before final captures so it does not cross the threshold. Original unrelated geometry and source ground retained.

limitations: Qualla public-domain corpus searched first. New portal construction follows the inspected original Daderot CC0 Casa Grande facade photograph; prior attribution-licensed imagery is excluded as a current control. Map/site layout and source ground retained; not an architectural or land survey.

The rectangular stone entrance has actual jamb/head reveals, threshold steps, recessed metal grille with arched fan and opaque inner boundary. Width, 0.55 m depth, levels and ornament are photographic estimates; interiors are not modeled.

Main facade and twin towers, rear wing layout, three guest-house footprints, pool temple/colonnades and terraced setting are retained. Fine carved figures, tile motifs, unseen window rhythms, interiors and complete garden ornament are generalized or omitted.
The 1941 aerial is supplementary layout evidence only. Modern exterior photographs control visible fabric; exact current roof services and restoration details remain uncertain.

Neptune pool center is mapped; basin dimensions come from California State Parks. Detailed curved perimeter, retaining joins and vertical terrace levels are interpretations, with unmodified host terrain retained for review.

Guest roofs and hidden sides are conservative approximations. Outlying service buildings, the broader estate, vegetation and zoo are outside this model. Reference photos are not embedded or redistributed.
